stem.text: An amino acid is a compound that has both an amine group and a carboxyl group.
The structures of three amino acids, P, Q and R, are shown in Figure 9.1.
Two of the amino acids in Figure 9.1 show stereoisomerism.
Draw the two stereoisomers of each of these amino acids in Figure 9.2. Name the type of stereoisomerism shown for each pair of stereoisomers. Use three-dimensional bonds where appropriate.

stem.caption: Figure 9.2
stem.alt: Two empty answer frames, each split into two boxes for a pair of stereoisomers, with a line 'type of stereoisomerism ....' under each pair.

guidance: Q may be given above, and P may be given below.
M3 conditional on optical linked to an attempt on P and geometrical / cistrans / EZ linked to an attempt on Q in M1 and M2.

points.text: M1 One pair of diagrams of P with correct use of 3D showing mirror images of two optical isomers
M2 One pair of diagrams showing correct E and Z of Q
M3 Optical or enantiomerism in the right place and Geometric(al) or E / Z or A cis/trans in the right place

figure.alt: From the MS: top, the two enantiomers of P (alanine), each a central C with COOH up, H and CH3, and NH2 on a wedge, drawn as mirror images either side of a dashed mirror line; bottom, the two geometrical isomers of Q, CH3(NH2)C=CH(COOH), one with COOH and CH3 on the same side and one with COOH on the opposite side.

explanation.text: P, NH<sub>2</sub>CH(CH<sub>3</sub>)COOH, has a carbon bonded to four different groups (H, CH<sub>3</sub>, NH<sub>2</sub>, COOH), so it is chiral and has two optical isomers (enantiomers). To draw them, use two bonds in the plane, one wedge and one hashed bond, then draw the mirror image.

Q, NH<sub>2</sub>C(CH<sub>3</sub>)=CHCOOH, has a C=C bond with two different groups on each carbon (NH<sub>2</sub>/CH<sub>3</sub> and H/COOH). Rotation about the π bond is restricted, so it has two geometrical (E/Z, cis/trans) isomers. They can be drawn flat, because the four groups lie in one plane.
R, glycine, has two H atoms on its only sp<sup>3</sup> carbon and no C=C, so it shows no stereoisomerism. M3 is for naming each type next to the right pair.

reasoningChain: Check each structure for a chiral carbon (four different groups) and for a C=C with two different groups on each end.
P: chiral centre, so draw two 3D mirror-image structures and label them optical.
Q: C=C with different groups on each carbon, so draw the E and Z isomers and label them geometrical (cis/trans).
R: neither feature, so leave it out.

inferredMistakes.text: Reading the formula of Q as having no double bond, because the ‘=’ is not printed in Figure 9.1, and looking for a chiral centre in it instead.
Drawing the two isomers of P without wedge / hashed bonds, or as two identical structures rather than mirror images.
Labelling the isomerism of P as geometrical or that of Q as optical; M3 needs each name next to the matching pair.

stem.text: The structures of amino acids T and U and their isoelectric points are shown in Table 9.1.

stem.caption: Table 9.1
stem.alt: Table 9.1. T: a five-membered ring with N-H (ring nitrogen) and a COOH on the carbon next to N (proline); isoelectric point 6.3. U: a benzene ring joined by CH2 to CH(NH2)COOH (phenylalanine); isoelectric point 5.5.

stem.text: Explain what is meant by isoelectric point.

guidance: A clear and correct description of zwitterion for second component.

points.text: the pH at which (the amino acid is) a zwitterion / no net charge / no overall charge / no total charge / electrically neutral / charge is neutral

explanation.text: An amino acid has an acidic –COOH group and a basic –NH<sub>2</sub> group, so its charge depends on pH. At low pH it is a cation (–NH<sub>3</sub><sup>+</sup>, –COOH); at high pH it is an anion (–NH<sub>2</sub>, –COO<sup>–</sup>). The isoelectric point is the particular pH at which it exists as the zwitterion, with equal + and – charges and no overall charge.

reasoningChain: Say it is a pH value.
Say that at this pH the amino acid has no net charge (zwitterion).

inferredMistakes.text: Leaving out ‘pH’, e.g. ‘when the amino acid is neutral’.
Saying the amino acid has ‘no charge’ at all, instead of no net or overall charge.

stem.text: Complete Table 9.2 to show the predominant species formed by amino acids T and U at the pH values shown.

guidance: two structures for one mark, four structures for two marks, six structures for three mark.
Phe at 5.5 can be (see figure, right)
Table left is repeated larger after 9(c)(iii).

points.text: T at pH 4.0: cation, ring N protonated (NH2+) and COOH
T at pH 5.5: cation, ring N protonated (NH2+) and COOH
T at pH 8.0: anion, ring NH and COO–
U at pH 4.0: cation, NH3+ and COOH
U at pH 5.5: zwitterion, NH3+ and COO–
U at pH 8.0: anion, NH2 and COO–

markScheme.note: The MS prints the answer as a table of six drawn structures; the six points describe them in words for reference. Any two correct structures earn 1 mark, four earn 2, six earn 3.

figure.alt: From the MS: left, the completed Table 9.2. T at pH 4.0 and 5.5: ring N protonated (NH2+) with COOH; at pH 8.0: ring NH with COO-. U at pH 4.0: H3N+ with COOH; at pH 5.5: H3N+ with COO-; at pH 8.0: NH2 with COO-. Right, from the Guidance column, the alternative accepted for U at pH 5.5: the un-ionised form with NH2 and COOH.

explanation.text: Compare each pH with the amino acid's isoelectric point (pI). Below the pI the species is a cation (amine protonated, COOH not ionised); at the pI it is the zwitterion; above the pI it is an anion (amine not protonated, COO<sup>–</sup>).

T (proline, pI 6.3): pH 4.0 and 5.5 are both below 6.3, so both are the cation; pH 8.0 is above, so the anion. U (phenylalanine, pI 5.5): pH 4.0 → cation, pH 5.5 = pI → zwitterion, pH 8.0 → anion. The MS also accepts the neutral un-ionised form of U at pH 5.5.
In T the nitrogen is in the ring, so when protonated it is –NH<sub>2</sub><sup>+</sup>– (secondary amine), not –NH<sub>3</sub><sup>+</sup>.

reasoningChain: T: pI 6.3; pH 4.0 and 5.5 are below → cation; pH 8.0 is above → anion.
U: pI 5.5; pH 4.0 → cation; pH 5.5 → zwitterion; pH 8.0 → anion.
Draw each structure: protonate the N for cations, ionise COOH to COO<sup>–</sup> for anions, both for the zwitterion.

inferredMistakes.text: Drawing T at pH 5.5 as a zwitterion, by using U's pI (5.5) instead of T's (6.3).
Drawing the ring nitrogen of T as –NH<sub>3</sub><sup>+</sup> (adding a third H) instead of –NH<sub>2</sub><sup>+</sup>–.
Reversing the rule, e.g. drawing anions below the pI and cations above it.

stem.text: Amino acids P, NH2CH(CH3)COOH, and R, NH2CH2COOH, can form tripeptide W, C8H15N3O4. The structure of tripeptide W can be represented as P–R–P.
Draw the structure of W. The peptide functional groups formed should be displayed.

points.text:
M2 – remainder is fully correct, e.g.
terminal groups not trailing bonds
neutral, zwitterion, 1+ or 1–
side/R groups CH3 – H – CH3
all H atoms on α-carbons

markScheme.note: The structure is printed as a drawing above M1.

figure.alt: Structure of W from the MS: H2N-CH(CH3)-C(=O)-NH-CH2-C(=O)-NH-CH(CH3)-COOH, with both peptide (C(=O)-N(H)) groups and all H atoms displayed.

explanation.text: Each peptide (amide) bond forms when the –COOH of one amino acid condenses with the –NH<sub>2</sub> of the next, losing H<sub>2</sub>O. P–R–P means alanine–glycine–alanine, read from the N-terminus.

‘Displayed’ means each –C(=O)–N(H)– group is drawn with every bond shown. The side groups are CH<sub>3</sub>, H, CH<sub>3</sub>, and the ends are a full NH<sub>2</sub> and COOH (or their ionised forms), not trailing bonds. Check with the formula: C<sub>8</sub>H<sub>15</sub>N<sub>3</sub>O<sub>4</sub>.

reasoningChain: Write the three residues in order: H<sub>2</sub>N–CH(CH<sub>3</sub>)–CO, NH–CH<sub>2</sub>–CO, NH–CH(CH<sub>3</sub>)–COOH.
Join them with two displayed peptide links, –C(=O)–N(H)–.
Check the side groups (CH<sub>3</sub>, H, CH<sub>3</sub>), the α-H atoms and the two ends, then count atoms against C<sub>8</sub>H<sub>15</sub>N<sub>3</sub>O<sub>4</sub>.

inferredMistakes.text: Writing the peptide links as condensed –CONH– instead of displaying the C=O and N–H bonds.
Leaving trailing bonds at the ends instead of complete NH<sub>2</sub> and COOH groups.
Missing an H on an α-carbon, or putting a CH<sub>3</sub> on the middle (glycine) residue.

stem.text: W reacts under suitable conditions to form two molecules of P and one molecule of R.

explanation.text: Breaking peptide bonds back into amino acids adds one H<sub>2</sub>O across each bond, so the reaction is hydrolysis, the reverse of the condensation that formed W. Saying whether it is acid, alkaline or enzymatic hydrolysis is ignored: the mark is for the word hydrolysis.

reasoningChain: W splits into its monomers: P + R + P.
Water is added across each peptide bond, so the reaction is hydrolysis.

inferredMistakes.text: Writing only ‘acid’ or ‘enzymatic’ without the word hydrolysis.

stem.text: Amino acids P and R can also form a number of polymers. One of these polymers, X, has a structure that can be represented as –[ P–R ]–n.
Name the type of polymerisation involved in the formation of X.

explanation.text: X is a polyamide (a polypeptide). Each link forms between –COOH and –NH<sub>2</sub> with loss of a small molecule (H<sub>2</sub>O), so this is condensation polymerisation. Addition polymerisation needs C=C monomers and loses nothing.

reasoningChain: Identify the link in X: an amide (peptide) bond between amino acids.
Forming it releases H<sub>2</sub>O, so it is condensation polymerisation.

inferredMistakes.text: Writing ‘addition-elimination’, which is a mechanism name; the MS ignores it.

issues.note: QP 上 Q 印作 'NH2C(CH3)CHCOOH'，没有印双键 '='；按 MS 9(a) M2（E/Z 异构）应为 NH2C(CH3)=CHCOOH。按原文照抄，未加 '='。Figure 9.1 只有三个文字式，用 table 块转录（caption 'Figure 9.1'）。

MS 答案是 6 个结构式组成的表，无法用文字表格转录；用 figure（左：答案表；右：Guidance 中 'Phe at 5.5 can be' 后的替代结构），6 个 point 是按图写的文字描述，方便引用。Guidance 'Table left is repeated larger after 9(c)(iii).' 照抄，但 MS PDF 在 9(c)(iii) 之后（p.21 是最后一页）并没有放大版表格。
'six structures for three mark.' 原文如此（mark 无 s），照抄。
9(a) 是 AS 有机立体异构（13.4），primary 13.4(5)（从结构式识别手性中心和顺反异构），secondary 13.4(3)、13.4(4)。
跨章题（13、34、35 章）。主线是氨基酸（等电点、肽键、水解），放在第 34 章（Nitrogen compounds，34.4 Amino acids）。
